addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Compliance Audit Log starter

A small, disposable starter for a local compliance audit-log service. The run
prompts grow it into a working service while preserving a stable CLI:

```text
python -m auditlog.cli record ACTOR ACTION OUTCOME --log-store STORE.db
python -m auditlog.cli query --actor ACTOR --log-store STORE.db
python -m auditlog.cli repair --log-store STORE.db
```

The trail is append-only. An entry, once recorded, is never removed, rewritten,
or reordered: corrections are made by recording a further entry, not by editing
history. Each entry carries a gapless `sequence` and an `event_id` derived
deterministically from the entry's own recorded content, so the same content
always yields the same id and any later edit is detectable by recomputing it.

Two log-store formats exist. The current format records each entry with an
explicit content-derived `event_id`. The older archive format used its own
`origin_ref` per entry and stored an export-observed `at` value rather than the
canonical recording time. It could renumber ids and restamp an event between
exports, so overlapping archive batches sometimes contain the same underlying
event twice with slightly different `at` values. Reading that format therefore
requires deciding when two archived entries are the same event and choosing one
representative timestamp deterministically.

`metadata` is caller-supplied descriptive context. It is never an input to an
entry's identity, and never an input to whether an entry is retained.

HTTP routing keeps request-path matching in `auditlog.paths` so
authentication and dispatch share one helper.

The initial scaffold only parses the command line. Implementing the store, the
append-only guarantees, recording, querying, integrity verification, and the
archive reader is the task.

The project must remain local-only and use the Python standard library. Tests use
`unittest`, so the environment needs no dependency installation.

1	"""Small starting model that later prompts are expected to extend.
2	
3	Only the shapes the acceptance path depends on live here: an audit entry, and
4	the canonical rule for deriving its id from its own recorded content. The run
5	prompts add the store, the append-only guarantees, querying, integrity
6	verification, and the archive reader.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import hashlib
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	from typing import Any
14	
15	# The fields that constitute an entry's identity. Anything outside this tuple
16	# is descriptive: it may differ between two records of the same event without
17	# making them different events.
18	IDENTIFYING_FIELDS: tuple[str, ...] = ("actor", "action", "outcome", "recorded_at")
19	
20	
21	def content_digest(actor: str, action: str, outcome: str, recorded_at: str) -> str:
22	    """Return the deterministic event id for this entry's recorded content.
23	
24	    Identity is the recorded content itself, so the same event recorded twice
25	    collapses to one id and any later edit to a stored entry is detectable by
26	    recomputing this. The separator cannot appear in a field value, so distinct
27	    inputs cannot collide by concatenation.
28	    """
29	
30	    joined = "\x1f".join((actor, action, outcome, recorded_at))
31	    return hashlib.sha256(joined.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

"""Small starting model that later prompts are expected to extend.

Only the shapes the acceptance path depends on live here: an audit entry, and
the canonical rule for deriving its id from its own recorded content. The run
prompts add the store, the append-only guarantees, querying, integrity
verification, and the archive reader.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

# The fields that constitute an entry's identity. Anything outside this tuple
# is descriptive: it may differ between two records of the same event without
# making them different events.
IDENTIFYING_FIELDS: tuple[str, ...] = ("actor", "action", "outcome", "recorded_at")


def content_digest(actor: str, action: str, outcome: str, recorded_at: str) -> str:
    """Return the deterministic event id for this entry's recorded content.

    Identity is the recorded content itself, so the same event recorded twice
    collapses to one id and any later edit to a stored entry is detectable by
    recomputing this. The separator cannot appear in a field value, so distinct
    inputs cannot collide by concatenation.
    """

    joined = "\x1f".join((actor, action, outcome, recorded_at))
    return hashlib.sha256(joined.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AuditEvent:
    """One recorded entry in the append-only trail.

    ``sequence`` is the entry's gapless position in the trail and ``event_id``
    is its content digest. ``source_version`` records which store format the
    entry was read from, and ``metadata`` carries caller-supplied context such
    as an archive's own reference. Both are descriptive: they explain an entry,
    and are never an input to its identity or to whether it is retained.
    """

    event_id: str
    sequence: int
    actor: str
    action: str
    outcome: str
    recorded_at: str
    source_version: int = 2
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def recomputed_id(self) -> str:
        """The id this entry's current content implies; compare to ``event_id``."""

        return content_digest(self.actor, self.action, self.outcome, self.recorded_at)

1	"""Storage-independent persistence for the audit trail.
2	
3	`AuditLogService` (see `auditlog.service`) only ever calls `read_all` and
4	`append` on whatever store it is given -- it never opens a file or checks
5	a format. Everything about *where* entries live, and which of the two
6	on-disk shapes they're in, stays behind this seam.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import json
12	from pathlib import Path
13	from typing import Protocol
14	
15	from auditlog.archive import normalize_legacy_entries
16	
17	CURRENT_STORE_VERSION = 2
18	LEGACY_STORE_VERSION = 1
19	
20	
21	class EventStore(Protocol):
22	    """Storage seam the service depends on instead of any concrete format."""
23	
24	    def read_all(self) -> list[dict]:
25	        """Return every stored entry as a plain dict, in stored order."""
26	
27	    def append(self, entry: dict) -> None:
28	        """Persist one more entry. Existing entries are never touched."""
29	
30	
31	class ReadOnlyStoreError(Exception):
32	    """Raised when `append` is called on a store that cannot accept writes."""
33	
34	
35	class JsonFileEventStore:
36	    """Current-format (`store_version` 2) log store: one JSON file, append-only."""
37	
38	    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
39	        self.path = path
40	
41	    def read_all(self) -> list[dict]:
42	        if not self.path.exists():
43	            return []
44	        payload = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
45	        return list(payload.get("entries", []))
46	
47	    def append(self, entry: dict) -> None:
48	        entries = self.read_all()
49	        entries.append(entry)
50	        payload = {"store_version": CURRENT_STORE_VERSION, "entries": entries}
51	        self.path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
52	
53	
54	class LegacyArchiveStore:
55	    """Read-only `store_version` 1 archive.
56	
57	    Callers always get normalized, current-shape dicts back (see
58	    `auditlog.archive`) -- never the raw `ref`/`at` shape -- so the rest
59	    of the service never has to know two formats exist.
60	    """
61	
62	    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
63	        self.path = path
64	
65	    def read_all(self) -> list[dict]:
66	        payload = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
67	        return normalize_legacy_entries(payload.get("entries", []))
68	
69	    def append(self, entry: dict) -> None:
70	        raise ReadOnlyStoreError(f"{self.path} is a legacy archive and cannot be appended to")
71	
72	
73	def open_store(path: Path) -> EventStore:
74	    """Sniff `path`'s `store_version` and return the matching store.
75	
76	    A path that doesn't exist yet is a fresh current-format store: the
77	    only way to create a `--log-store` is to `record` into it.
78	    """
79	
80	    if not path.exists():
81	        return JsonFileEventStore(path)
82	    payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
83	    version = payload.get("store_version", CURRENT_STORE_VERSION)
84	    if version == LEGACY_STORE_VERSION:
85	        return LegacyArchiveStore(path)
86	    if version == CURRENT_STORE_VERSION:
87	        return JsonFileEventStore(path)
88	    raise ValueError(f"unsupported store_version {version!r} in {path}")

"""Storage-independent audit trail service.

Everything here works against the `EventStore` protocol in
`auditlog.storage`. It never opens a file, never checks a `store_version`,
and never knows whether it's talking to the current format, the legacy
archive, or something else entirely -- swapping the backend never
requires touching this module.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timezone

from auditlog.models import AuditEvent
from auditlog.models import content_digest as compute_event_id
from auditlog.storage import CURRENT_STORE_VERSION, EventStore


class SequenceError(Exception):
    """A store's entries are not a gapless 1..N sequence."""


class IntegrityError(Exception):
    """A stored entry's content no longer matches its recorded event id."""


def _to_event(raw: dict, index: int) -> AuditEvent:
    return AuditEvent(
        event_id=raw["event_id"],
        sequence=raw.get("sequence", index + 1),
        actor=raw["actor"],
        action=raw["action"],
        outcome=raw["outcome"],
        recorded_at=raw["recorded_at"],
        source_version=raw.get("source_version", CURRENT_STORE_VERSION),
        metadata=raw.get("metadata", {}),
    )


class AuditLogService:
    """Record, query, and verify an append-only trail on any `EventStore`."""

    def __init__(self, store: EventStore) -> None:
        self.store = store

    def events(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        """Every entry, normalized and ordered by sequence."""

        raw = self.store.read_all()
        parsed = [_to_event(entry, index) for index, entry in enumerate(raw)]
        return sorted(parsed, key=lambda event: event.sequence)

    def record(
        self,
        actor: str,
        action: str,
        outcome: str,
        metadata: dict | None = None,
        recorded_at: str | None = None,
    ) -> AuditEvent:
        """Append one entry. Its id is derived only from its own content."""

        sequence = len(self.events()) + 1
        recorded_at = recorded_at or datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
        raw = {
            "event_id": compute_event_id(actor, action, outcome, recorded_at),
            "sequence": sequence,
            "actor": actor,
            "action": action,
            "outcome": outcome,
            "recorded_at": recorded_at,
            "source_version": CURRENT_STORE_VERSION,
            "metadata": metadata or {},
        }
        self.store.append(raw)
        return _to_event(raw, sequence - 1)

    def query(self, actor: str | None = None, action: str | None = None) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        """Entries matching the given filters, in sequence order."""

        return [
            event
            for event in self.events()
            if (actor is None or event.actor == actor)
            and (action is None or event.action == action)
        ]

    def verify(self) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        """Check the trail is gapless and untampered; return it if so.

        Sequence is checked first: a missing or reordered entry is a
        structural break in the trail regardless of content. Content is
        checked second, only once the position it's being checked at is
        already known to be correct.
        """

        events = self.events()
        for index, event in enumerate(events, start=1):
            if event.sequence != index:
                raise SequenceError(
                    f"expected sequence {index} at position {index}, found {event.sequence}"
                )
            if event.recomputed_id() != event.event_id:
                raise IntegrityError(
                    f"entry at sequence {event.sequence} no longer matches its recorded content"
                )
        return events

"""Command-line shell for the audit log service."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from auditlog.service import AuditLogService, IntegrityError, SequenceError
from auditlog.storage import ReadOnlyStoreError, open_store


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Return the stable top-level parser the acceptance path imports.

    The ``record``/``query``/``repair`` commands and their required
    ``--log-store`` option are the documented contract; keep them.
    """

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="auditlog")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    record = subparsers.add_parser("record", help="append an entry to the trail")
    record.add_argument("actor")
    record.add_argument("action")
    record.add_argument("outcome")
    record.add_argument(
        "--metadata",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        metavar="KEY=VALUE",
        help="descriptive context to store with the entry; repeatable",
    )
    record.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)

    query = subparsers.add_parser("query", help="read entries from the trail")
    query.add_argument("--actor")
    query.add_argument("--action")
    query.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)

    repair = subparsers.add_parser("repair", help="rebuild derived indexes")
    repair.add_argument("--log-store", required=True)
    return parser


def _parse_metadata(pairs: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    metadata: dict[str, str] = {}
    for pair in pairs:
        key, sep, value = pair.partition("=")
        if not sep:
            raise ValueError(f"--metadata expects KEY=VALUE, got {pair!r}")
        metadata[key] = value
    return metadata


def _print_event(event) -> None:
    print(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "event_id": event.event_id,
                "sequence": event.sequence,
                "actor": event.actor,
                "action": event.action,
                "outcome": event.outcome,
                "recorded_at": event.recorded_at,
                "source_version": event.source_version,
                "metadata": event.metadata,
            }
        )
    )


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Parse the command line and run the requested command."""

    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    service = AuditLogService(open_store(Path(args.log_store)))

    if args.command == "record":
        try:
            metadata = _parse_metadata(args.metadata)
        except ValueError as exc:
            parser.error(str(exc))
        try:
            event = service.record(args.actor, args.action, args.outcome, metadata)
        except ReadOnlyStoreError as exc:
            parser.error(str(exc))
        _print_event(event)
        return 0

    if args.command == "query":
        for event in service.query(actor=args.actor, action=args.action):
            _print_event(event)
        return 0

    if args.command == "repair":
        try:
            events = service.verify()
        except (SequenceError, IntegrityError) as exc:
            print(f"repair: trail is broken: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print(f"repair: {len(events)} entries verified, trail intact")
        return 0

    parser.error(f"the {args.command!r} command is not implemented yet")
    return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

4	changes which route version -- v1 or v2 -- a request is dispatched to.
5	It never changes whether the route requires a bearer token: that

8	alias (`auditlog.httpd.resolve_v2_alias_catalog`). `bearer_required` below
9	is the assertion that both phases resolve to the same answer.

21	# changes between phases. Matches fixtures/phase-route-expectations.yaml.

33	    with csv_path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
34	        for row in csv.DictReader(handle):
35	            if row["enabled"].strip().lower() == "true":
36	                phases[row["cohort"]] = row["phase"]

41	    """The (method, path) a cohort in `phase` uses for `action`."""
42	
43	    method, suffix = ACTION_ROUTES[action]
44	    return method, f"/{phase}{suffix}"
45

48	    """Canonical bearer requirements for every V1 route plus every V2 alias."""
49	
50	    table = dict(CANONICAL_V1_BEARER)
51	    resolved = resolve_v2_alias_catalog(build_v2_alias_catalog(), CANONICAL_V1_BEARER)
52	    for method, path, _permission, requires_auth in resolved:

61	    It never changes this answer: `bearer_required(action, "v1")` and
62	    `bearer_required(action, "v2")` always agree for the same action.
63	    """

def load_cohort_phases(csv_path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return {cohort: phase} for enabled rows of an upgrade-cohorts.csv file."""

    phases: dict[str, str] = {}
    with csv_path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for row in csv.DictReader(handle):
            if row["enabled"].strip().lower() == "true":
                phases[row["cohort"]] = row["phase"]
    return phases


def route_for(action: str, phase: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """The (method, path) a cohort in `phase` uses for `action`."""

    method, suffix = ACTION_ROUTES[action]
    return method, f"/{phase}{suffix}"


def bearer_table() -> dict[tuple[str, str], bool]:
    """Canonical bearer requirements for every V1 route plus every V2 alias."""

    table = dict(CANONICAL_V1_BEARER)
    resolved = resolve_v2_alias_catalog(build_v2_alias_catalog(), CANONICAL_V1_BEARER)
    for method, path, _permission, requires_auth in resolved:
        table[(method, path)] = requires_auth
    return table


def bearer_required(action: str, phase: str) -> bool:
    """Whether `action` requires a bearer token when routed through `phase`.

    Cohort selection picks `phase`, which changes only the resolved path.
    It never changes this answer: `bearer_required(action, "v1")` and
    `bearer_required(action, "v2")` always agree for the same action.
    """

    method, path = route_for(action, phase)
    return bearer_table()[(method, path)]

"""Canonical V1 bearer requirements and the V2 alias catalog that inherits them.

Phase selection (see `auditlog.cohorts`) picks which of these a cohort's
requests resolve to; it never assigns a bearer requirement of its own.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

# The bearer requirement for each V1 route. This is the one place a route's
# auth requirement is ever set directly.
CANONICAL_V1_BEARER: dict[tuple[str, str], bool] = {
    ("POST", "/v1/entries"): True,
    ("GET", "/v1/entries"): True,
    ("GET", "/v1/integrity"): True,

def build_v2_alias_catalog() -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...]:
    """Return every planned V2 alias, inheriting its bearer requirement from V1.

    ``None`` means "inherit": a V2 alias never states its own bearer
    requirement, it only ever takes on its canonical V1 route's requirement
    (resolved by `auditlog.httpd.resolve_v2_alias_catalog`).
    """

    return (
        ("POST", "/v2/entries", "record", None),
        ("GET", "/v2/entries", "query", None),
        ("GET", "/v2/integrity", "integrity", None),
    )

"""Normalizes the legacy (`store_version` 1) archive format.

The archive format re-exports events with its own `ref` and an
export-observed `at`, not the canonical recording time. The same
underlying event can appear more than once across overlapping export
batches with a slightly different `at` each time -- see
fixtures/legacy-events.json, where the first two entries are the same
policy.update event re-exported two seconds apart. Duplicates never share
a `ref`, so `ref` cannot be the dedupe key, and `metadata` is
caller-supplied context, never identity (see
`auditlog.models.IDENTIFYING_FIELDS`). Content plus proximity in time is
the only signal available, so entries sharing (actor, action, outcome)
within `DEDUPE_WINDOW` of each other are folded into one event.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

from auditlog.models import content_digest

# Two exports of the same event land close together; two independent
# occurrences of the same actor/action/outcome do not. Chosen generously
# above the 2-second drift in the seed fixture and well below any
# realistic gap between unrelated occurrences of the same action.
DEDUPE_WINDOW = timedelta(minutes=5)


def _parse_at(value: str) -> datetime:
    return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))


def normalize_legacy_entries(raw_entries: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Collapse export duplicates and return canonical current-shape entries.

    Entries are grouped by (actor, action, outcome), then split into
    clusters wherever consecutive `at` values (sorted ascending) are more
    than `DEDUPE_WINDOW` apart; each cluster is one underlying event. The
    representative `recorded_at` is the earliest `at` in its cluster --
    the export closest to the true recording time -- so the result does
    not depend on the order entries were read in or how export batches
    happened to overlap.
    """

    groups: dict[tuple[str, str, str], list[dict]] = {}
    for raw in raw_entries:
        key = (raw["actor"], raw["action"], raw["outcome"])
        groups.setdefault(key, []).append(raw)

    events: list[dict] = []
    for (actor, action, outcome), members in groups.items():
        ordered = sorted(members, key=lambda member: _parse_at(member["at"]))
        cluster: list[dict] = []
        for member in ordered:
            if cluster and _parse_at(member["at"]) - _parse_at(cluster[-1]["at"]) > DEDUPE_WINDOW:
                events.append(_build_event(actor, action, outcome, cluster))
                cluster = []
            cluster.append(member)
        if cluster:
            events.append(_build_event(actor, action, outcome, cluster))

    events.sort(key=lambda event: event["recorded_at"])
    return events


def _build_event(actor: str, action: str, outcome: str, cluster: list[dict]) -> dict:
    recorded_at = min(member["at"] for member in cluster)
    return {
        "event_id": content_digest(actor, action, outcome, recorded_at),
        "actor": actor,
        "action": action,
        "outcome": outcome,
        "recorded_at": recorded_at,
        "source_version": 1,
        "metadata": {"origin_refs": [member["ref"] for member in cluster]},
    }

1	"""Request-path helpers shared by authentication and dispatch.
2	
3	Versioned routes and proxy spellings should pass through one helper so a
4	documented path and a harmless alternate spelling reach the same decision.
5	"""
6	from __future__ import annotations
7	
8	from urllib.parse import unquote
9	
10	
11	def canonical_path(raw_path: str) -> str:
12	    """Compatibility spelling: decode, collapse slashes, drop one trailing slash."""
13	
14	    path = unquote(raw_path)
15	    while "//" in path:
16	        path = path.replace("//", "/")
17	    if len(path) > 1:
18	        path = path.rstrip("/")
19	    return path or "/"
20	
21	
22	def auth_path(raw_path: str) -> str:
23	    """Path used to look up the route table before reading a body."""
24	
25	    # Look up the route using the same path spelling the rest of the service uses.
26	    return canonical_path(raw_path)
27	
28	
29	def dispatch_path(raw_path: str) -> str:
30	    """Path handed to the handler after the route decision."""
31	
32	    # Hand the handler the same path the route lookup used.
33	    return auth_path(raw_path)

"""Tests for the storage seam: format sniffing, round-tripping, read-only archive."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from auditlog.storage import (
    JsonFileEventStore,
    LegacyArchiveStore,
    ReadOnlyStoreError,
    open_store,
)

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "fixtures"


class OpenStoreTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_missing_path_opens_a_fresh_current_store(self) -> None:
        store = open_store(Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "does-not-exist.db")
        self.assertIsInstance(store, JsonFileEventStore)
        self.assertEqual(store.read_all(), [])

    def test_current_format_fixture_opens_a_json_file_store(self) -> None:
        store = open_store(FIXTURES / "current-events.json")
        self.assertIsInstance(store, JsonFileEventStore)

    def test_legacy_format_fixture_opens_a_legacy_archive_store(self) -> None:
        store = open_store(FIXTURES / "legacy-events.json")
        self.assertIsInstance(store, LegacyArchiveStore)


class JsonFileEventStoreTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.tmp_dir)
        self.path = self.tmp_dir / "store.db"

    def test_append_then_read_all_round_trips(self) -> None:
        store = JsonFileEventStore(self.path)
        entry = {"event_id": "abc", "sequence": 1, "actor": "a", "action": "b",
                  "outcome": "allowed", "recorded_at": "T1", "source_version": 2, "metadata": {}}
        store.append(entry)

        reloaded = JsonFileEventStore(self.path)
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.read_all(), [entry])

    def test_appending_never_rewrites_earlier_entries(self) -> None:
        store = JsonFileEventStore(self.path)
        first = {"event_id": "1", "sequence": 1, "actor": "a", "action": "b",
                  "outcome": "allowed", "recorded_at": "T1", "source_version": 2, "metadata": {}}
        second = {"event_id": "2", "sequence": 2, "actor": "a", "action": "b",
                   "outcome": "denied", "recorded_at": "T2", "source_version": 2, "metadata": {}}
        store.append(first)
        store.append(second)

        on_disk = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(on_disk["entries"], [first, second])


class LegacyArchiveStoreTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_read_all_returns_normalized_entries(self) -> None:
        store = LegacyArchiveStore(FIXTURES / "legacy-events.json")
        events = store.read_all()
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 3)
        self.assertTrue(all("event_id" in event for event in events))

    def test_append_is_rejected(self) -> None:
        store = LegacyArchiveStore(FIXTURES / "legacy-events.json")
        with self.assertRaises(ReadOnlyStoreError):
            store.append({"actor": "x", "action": "y", "outcome": "z", "recorded_at": "T"})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Tests for the storage-independent AuditLogService."""

from __future__ import annotations

import unittest

from auditlog.models import content_digest
from auditlog.service import AuditLogService, IntegrityError, SequenceError


class InMemoryStore:
    """A minimal EventStore with no relation to JSON files or disk at all.

    Exercising the service against this instead of JsonFileEventStore is
    the check that the service is genuinely storage-independent.
    """

    def __init__(self, entries=None) -> None:
        self.entries = list(entries or [])

    def read_all(self):
        return list(self.entries)

    def append(self, entry):
        self.entries.append(entry)


class RecordTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_record_assigns_a_gapless_sequence(self) -> None:
        service = AuditLogService(InMemoryStore())
        first = service.record("operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed", recorded_at="T1")
        second = service.record("operator:mina", "policy.update", "denied", recorded_at="T2")
        self.assertEqual((first.sequence, second.sequence), (1, 2))

    def test_recorded_event_id_matches_its_own_content(self) -> None:
        service = AuditLogService(InMemoryStore())
        event = service.record("operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed", recorded_at="T1")
        self.assertEqual(event.event_id, event.recomputed_id())

    def test_metadata_does_not_affect_the_event_id(self) -> None:
        service = AuditLogService(InMemoryStore())
        without = service.record("a", "b", "c", recorded_at="T1")
        service2 = AuditLogService(InMemoryStore())
        with_metadata = service2.record("a", "b", "c", metadata={"note": "x"}, recorded_at="T1")
        self.assertEqual(without.event_id, with_metadata.event_id)


class QueryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_query_filters_by_actor_and_action(self) -> None:
        service = AuditLogService(InMemoryStore())
        service.record("operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed", recorded_at="T1")
        service.record("service:indexer", "report.read", "allowed", recorded_at="T2")
        service.record("operator:mina", "key.revoke", "allowed", recorded_at="T3")

        by_actor = service.query(actor="operator:mina")
        self.assertEqual({e.action for e in by_actor}, {"policy.update", "key.revoke"})

        by_action = service.query(action="report.read")
        self.assertEqual([e.actor for e in by_action], ["service:indexer"])

    def test_query_results_are_sequence_ordered(self) -> None:
        service = AuditLogService(InMemoryStore())
        service.record("a", "x", "allowed", recorded_at="T1")
        service.record("a", "y", "allowed", recorded_at="T2")
        sequences = [e.sequence for e in service.query(actor="a")]
        self.assertEqual(sequences, sorted(sequences))


class VerifyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_verify_passes_an_intact_trail(self) -> None:
        service = AuditLogService(InMemoryStore())
        service.record("a", "x", "allowed", recorded_at="T1")
        service.record("a", "y", "allowed", recorded_at="T2")
        self.assertEqual(len(service.verify()), 2)

    def test_verify_detects_a_sequence_gap(self) -> None:
        store = InMemoryStore(
            [
                {"event_id": content_digest("a", "x", "allowed", "T1"), "sequence": 1,
                 "actor": "a", "action": "x", "outcome": "allowed", "recorded_at": "T1",
                 "source_version": 2, "metadata": {}},
                {"event_id": content_digest("a", "y", "allowed", "T2"), "sequence": 3,
                 "actor": "a", "action": "y", "outcome": "allowed", "recorded_at": "T2",
                 "source_version": 2, "metadata": {}},
            ]
        )
        service = AuditLogService(store)
        with self.assertRaises(SequenceError):
            service.verify()

    def test_verify_detects_a_tampered_entry(self) -> None:
        service = AuditLogService(InMemoryStore())
        service.record("a", "x", "allowed", recorded_at="T1")
        # Simulate an edit made directly to storage rather than through record().
        service.store.entries[0]["outcome"] = "denied"
        with self.assertRaises(IntegrityError):
            service.verify()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""End-to-end tests for the record/query/repair CLI commands."""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import shutil
import tempfile
import unittest
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from pathlib import Path

from auditlog.cli import main


class CliTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.tmp_dir)
        self.store_path = self.tmp_dir / "store.db"

    def _run(self, argv: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str]:
        buffer = io.StringIO()
        with redirect_stdout(buffer):
            code = main(argv)
        return code, buffer.getvalue()

    def test_record_then_query_round_trips(self) -> None:
        code, _ = self._run(
            ["record", "operator:mina", "policy.update", "allowed", "--log-store", str(self.store_path)]
        )
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)

        code, out = self._run(["query", "--actor", "operator:mina", "--log-store", str(self.store_path)])
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        event = json.loads(out.strip())
        self.assertEqual(event["actor"], "operator:mina")
        self.assertEqual(event["sequence"], 1)

    def test_repair_reports_an_intact_trail(self) -> None:
        self._run(["record", "a", "x", "allowed", "--log-store", str(self.store_path)])
        self._run(["record", "a", "y", "allowed", "--log-store", str(self.store_path)])

        code, out = self._run(["repair", "--log-store", str(self.store_path)])
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIn("2 entries verified", out)

    def test_repair_detects_a_tampered_store(self) -> None:
        self._run(["record", "a", "x", "allowed", "--log-store", str(self.store_path)])
        payload = json.loads(self.store_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        payload["entries"][0]["outcome"] = "denied"
        self.store_path.write_text(json.dumps(payload), encoding="utf-8")

        code, _ = self._run(["repair", "--log-store", str(self.store_path)])
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)

    def test_metadata_is_stored_but_never_changes_the_event_id(self) -> None:
        code, out = self._run(
            [
                "record", "a", "x", "allowed",
                "--metadata", "note=first",
                "--log-store", str(self.store_path),
            ]
        )
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        event = json.loads(out.strip())
        self.assertEqual(event["metadata"], {"note": "first"})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Tests for normalizing the legacy archive format."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from auditlog.archive import normalize_legacy_entries
from auditlog.models import content_digest


class NormalizeLegacyEntriesTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        fixture_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "fixtures" / "legacy-events.json"
        self.raw_entries = json.loads(fixture_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["entries"]

    def test_export_duplicates_collapse_to_one_event(self) -> None:
        events = normalize_legacy_entries(self.raw_entries)

        # Four archive rows, but the first two are the same policy.update
        # event re-exported two seconds apart, so three events remain.
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 3)

        merged = next(e for e in events if e["action"] == "policy.update")
        self.assertEqual(merged["recorded_at"], "2024-03-02T10:15:00Z")
        self.assertEqual(sorted(merged["metadata"]["origin_refs"]), ["arch-1001", "arch-2001"])

    def test_representative_timestamp_is_deterministic_regardless_of_order(self) -> None:
        forward = normalize_legacy_entries(self.raw_entries)
        backward = normalize_legacy_entries(list(reversed(self.raw_entries)))

        by_action = lambda events: {e["action"]: e["recorded_at"] for e in events}
        self.assertEqual(by_action(forward), by_action(backward))

    def test_event_id_is_derived_from_the_chosen_content(self) -> None:
        events = normalize_legacy_entries(self.raw_entries)
        merged = next(e for e in events if e["action"] == "policy.update")

        expected_id = content_digest(
            merged["actor"], merged["action"], merged["outcome"], merged["recorded_at"]
        )
        self.assertEqual(merged["event_id"], expected_id)

    def test_far_apart_repeats_of_the_same_content_stay_distinct(self) -> None:
        raw = [
            {"ref": "a", "actor": "operator:mina", "action": "login", "outcome": "allowed",
             "at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
            {"ref": "b", "actor": "operator:mina", "action": "login", "outcome": "allowed",
             "at": "2024-01-02T00:00:00Z"},
        ]
        events = normalize_legacy_entries(raw)
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""HTTP transport for the audit log: alias resolution, and the V1 daemon.

`resolve_v2_alias_catalog` is the stable alias-resolution seam described
below. Everything past it is the actual network daemon: a bearer-protected
V1 `record`/`query`/`integrity` API backed by SQLite persistence. Only the
routes in `ROUTE_ACTIONS` (mirroring `auditlog.policy.CANONICAL_V1_BEARER`)
are ever dispatched to -- the V2 alias catalog in
`auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog` is resolved here for callers such
as `auditlog.cohorts`, but no V2 path is installed on the live server yet.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import sqlite3
import threading
from http import HTTPStatus
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit

from auditlog.paths import auth_path, dispatch_path
from auditlog.policy import CANONICAL_V1_BEARER
from auditlog.service import AuditLogService, IntegrityError, SequenceError


def resolve_v2_alias_catalog(catalog: tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...], canonical_bearer: dict[tuple[str, str], bool]) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool], ...]:
    """Resolve inherited aliases through their canonical V1 route keys."""

    resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str, bool]] = []
    for method, path, permission, requires_auth in catalog:
        if requires_auth is None:
            canonical_path = path.replace("/v2/", "/v1/", 1)
            requires_auth = canonical_bearer.get((method, canonical_path), True)
        resolved.append((method, path, permission, requires_auth))
    return tuple(resolved)


# The only routes the live daemon dispatches to. Keys match
# `auditlog.policy.CANONICAL_V1_BEARER` exactly: every installed route has a
# canonical bearer requirement, and every canonical requirement names an
# installed route. There is no V2 entry here -- installing the V2 alias
# catalog at runtime is a later prompt's job.
ROUTE_ACTIONS: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {
    ("POST", "/v1/entries"): "record",
    ("GET", "/v1/entries"): "query",

            """

                sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
                event_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                actor TEXT NOT NULL,
                action TEXT NOT NULL,

"""Tests for the V1 HTTP daemon: SQLite persistence, bearer auth, cohorts."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
from http.client import HTTPConnection
from pathlib import Path

from auditlog.httpd import ROUTE_ACTIONS, SqliteEventStore, build_server, load_cohort_configuration
from auditlog.policy import CANONICAL_V1_BEARER

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "fixtures"
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent
TOKEN = "s3cr3t-test-token"  # noqa: S105 - test fixture, not a real secret


class SqliteEventStoreTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """SQLite persistence: round-trips, re-open, and separate-process reads."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.tmp_dir)
        self.path = self.tmp_dir / "store.sqlite3"

    def test_append_then_read_all_round_trips(self) -> None:
        store = SqliteEventStore(self.path)
        entry = {
            "event_id": "abc", "sequence": 1, "actor": "a", "action": "b",
            "outcome": "allowed", "recorded_at": "T1", "source_version": 2,
            "metadata": {"k": "v"},
        }
        store.append(entry)
        self.assertEqual(store.read_all(), [entry])

    def test_appending_never_rewrites_earlier_entries(self) -> None:
        store = SqliteEventStore(self.path)
        first = {"event_id": "1", "sequence": 1, "actor": "a", "action": "b",
                 "outcome": "allowed", "recorded_at": "T1", "source_version": 2, "metadata": {}}
        second = {"event_id": "2", "sequence": 2, "actor": "a", "action": "b",
                  "outcome": "denied", "recorded_at": "T2", "source_version": 2, "metadata": {}}
        store.append(first)
        store.append(second)
        self.assertEqual(store.read_all(), [first, second])

    def test_reopening_the_same_path_sees_prior_writes(self) -> None:
        SqliteEventStore(self.path).append(
            {"event_id": "1", "sequence": 1, "actor": "a", "action": "b",
             "outcome": "allowed", "recorded_at": "T1", "source_version": 2, "metadata": {}}
        )
        reopened = SqliteEventStore(self.path)
        self.assertEqual(len(reopened.read_all()), 1)

    def test_read_all_from_a_separate_process_sees_committed_entries(self) -> None:
        store = SqliteEventStore(self.path)
        store.append(
            {"event_id": "1", "sequence": 1, "actor": "operator:mina",
             "action": "policy.update", "outcome": "allowed", "recorded_at": "T1",
             "source_version": 2, "metadata": {}}
        )
        store.append(
            {"event_id": "2", "sequence": 2, "actor": "operator:mina",
             "action": "policy.update", "outcome": "denied", "recorded_at": "T2",
             "source_version": 2, "metadata": {}}
        )

        script = (
            "import json\n"
            "from auditlog.httpd import SqliteEventStore\n"
            f"print(json.dumps(SqliteEventStore({str(self.path)!r}).read_all()))\n"
        )
        completed = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-c", script],
            cwd=REPO_ROOT,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        )
        entries = json.loads(completed.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(len(entries), 2)
        self.assertEqual([e["actor"] for e in entries], ["operator:mina", "operator:mina"])
        self.assertEqual([e["outcome"] for e in entries], ["allowed", "denied"])


class LoadCohortConfigurationTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Deterministic cohort configuration loaded from the supplied CSV."""

    def test_enabled_cohorts_map_to_their_phase(self) -> None:
        phases = load_cohort_configuration(FIXTURES / "upgrade-cohorts.csv")
        self.assertEqual(phases, {"canary-a": "v2", "control-a": "v1"})

    def test_output_is_deterministic_across_calls(self) -> None:
        first = load_cohort_configuration(FIXTURES / "upgrade-cohorts.csv")
        second = load_cohort_configuration(FIXTURES / "upgrade-cohorts.csv")
        self.assertEqual(first, second)


class LiveServerTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    """Starts one real V1-only daemon per test against a temp SQLite store."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.tmp_dir)
        self.server = build_server(
            self.tmp_dir / "store.sqlite3",
            bearer_token=TOKEN,
            cohorts_csv=FIXTURES / "upgrade-cohorts.csv",
            port=0,
        )
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
        self.addCleanup(self._shutdown)
        self.host, self.port = self.server.server_address

    def _shutdown(self) -> None:
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()
        self.thread.join(timeout=5)

    def _request(
        self,
        method: str,
        path: str,
        *,
        token: str | None = None,
        body: dict | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[int, dict | None]:
        conn = HTTPConnection(self.host, self.port, timeout=5)
        try:
            headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
            if token is not None:
                headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
            payload = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8") if body is not None else b""
            conn.request(method, path, body=payload, headers=headers)
            response = conn.getresponse()
            raw = response.read()
            data = json.loads(raw) if raw else None
            return response.status, data
        finally:
            conn.close()


class BearerProtectedRouteTests(LiveServerTestCase):
    def test_record_then_query_round_trips_over_http(self) -> None:
        status, created = self._request(
            "POST", "/v1/entries", token=TOKEN,
            body={"actor": "operator:mina", "action": "policy.update", "outcome": "allowed",
                  "recorded_at": "T1"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201)
        self.assertEqual(created["sequence"], 1)

        status, result = self._request("GET", "/v1/entries?actor=operator%3Amina", token=TOKEN)
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual([e["actor"] for e in result["entries"]], ["operator:mina"])

    def test_integrity_reports_an_intact_trail(self) -> None:
        self._request(
            "POST", "/v1/entries", token=TOKEN,
            body={"actor": "a", "action": "x", "outcome": "allowed", "recorded_at": "T1"},
        )
        status, result = self._request("GET", "/v1/integrity", token=TOKEN)
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertTrue(result["verified"])
        self.assertEqual(result["count"], 1)


class RefusalTests(LiveServerTestCase):
    def test_missing_bearer_token_is_refused_on_every_v1_route(self) -> None:
        for method, path in CANONICAL_V1_BEARER:
            with self.subTest(method=method, path=path):
                status, _ = self._request(method, path)
                self.assertEqual(status, 401)

    def test_wrong_bearer_token_is_refused(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request("GET", "/v1/entries", token="not-the-token")
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)

    def test_correct_bearer_token_is_accepted(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self._request("GET", "/v1/entries", token=TOKEN)
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)

    def test_refusal_never_reaches_the_store(self) -> None:
        self._request(
            "POST", "/v1/entries", token="wrong",
            body={"actor": "a", "action": "x", "outcome": "allowed"},
        )
        status, result = self._request("GET", "/v1/entries", token=TOKEN)
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(result["entries"], [])


class CohortConfigurationTests(LiveServerTestCase):
    def test_cohort_phases_are_loaded_deterministically_from_the_csv(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(self.server.cohort_phases, {"canary-a": "v2", "control-a": "v1"})

    def test_only_v1_routes_are_installed_regardless_of_cohort_phase(self) -> None:
        # canary-a is configured for v2, but no v2 route exists on the live server.
        self.assertTrue(all(path.startswith("/v1/") for _method, path in ROUTE_ACTIONS))
        status, _ = self._request("GET", "/v2/entries", token=TOKEN)
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

All 53 tests pass. Summary of what was done:

**`auditlog/httpd.py`** — added, alongside the existing `resolve_v2_alias_catalog` alias seam:
- `SqliteEventStore`: an `EventStore`-compatible SQLite backend (WAL mode, autocommit, one connection per thread) for the daemon's persistence.
- `ROUTE_ACTIONS`: the only routes ever dispatched — the three V1 routes, keyed identically to `auditlog.policy.CANONICAL_V1_BEARER`. No V2 entry exists here.
- `V1RequestHandler`/`AuditHTTPServer`: a real bearer-protected HTTP daemon for `record`/`query`/`integrity`, using `auth_path`/`dispatch_path` from `auditlog.paths` for the pre-body auth decision and the post-decision dispatch respectively (auth is checked before any request body is read, so a refused request never reaches the store).
- `load_cohort_configuration`: a deterministic CSV loader kept separate from `auditlog.cohorts.load_cohort_phases` specifically to avoid a circular import (`cohorts.py` already imports from `httpd.py`). `build_server` loads it for a later phase to consult, but it never installs a route.

**`auditlog/policy.py`** — `build_v2_alias_catalog()` now returns the three fixed V2 rows with explicit `True` bearer values (not the old `None`-inherit sentinel), with docstrings updated to match. This is backward-compatible with `resolve_v2_alias_catalog` and `auditlog.cohorts.bearer_table()`, which still work unchanged.

**Tests** — `tests/test_policy.py` (catalog output, explicit-`True` check, determinism, not-installed) and `tests/test_httpd.py` (SQLite round-trip/reopen/**separate-process** read via a `subprocess`, bearer refusal on every V1 route including "refusal never reaches the store," and deterministic cohort config loading tied to the live server).

No existing file's behavior changed for callers other than `build_v2_alias_catalog`'s bearer values going from `None`→`True` (a strictly compatible change, verified by the full pre-existing suite still passing).

   - Append-only audit trail with content-derived `event_id` (SHA-256 digest of `actor|action|outcome|recorded_at` joined by `\x1f`), gapless `sequence` numbers, `SequenceError`/`IntegrityError` verification.
   - Storage-independent `AuditLogService` operating only against an `EventStore` Protocol (`read_all`/`append`) — used as a design invariant that must be preserved for any new storage backend.
   - Two existing on-disk formats: current (`store_version=2`, `JsonFileEventStore`) and legacy archive (`store_version=1`, `LegacyArchiveStore`, read-only, deduplicates via `normalize_legacy_entries`/`DEDUPE_WINDOW`).
   - Phased API upgrade: V1 canonical routes vs. V2 alias routes; cohort-to-phase mapping via CSV (`fixtures/upgrade-cohorts.csv`); the architectural invariant that **cohort/phase selection changes only which path prefix (v1/v2) a request resolves to, and NEVER changes whether a bearer token is required** — this invariant is asserted by `auditlog.cohorts.bearer_required()` and now more directly by `auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog()`'s explicit `True` values.
   - `CANONICAL_V1_BEARER: dict[tuple[str,str], bool]` in `policy.py` as the single source of truth for which (method, path) pairs require a bearer token.
   - V2 alias catalog: `tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...]` shape = (method, path, permission-name, requires_auth). `None` was formerly used as an "inherit from V1" sentinel resolved by `resolve_v2_alias_catalog`; now changed to explicit `True` per the user's latest instruction.
   - **Critical one-directional import constraint discovered**: `auditlog/cohorts.py` imports `resolve_v2_alias_catalog` from `auditlog.httpd` and `CANONICAL_V1_BEARER, build_v2_alias_catalog` from `auditlog.policy`. Therefore `auditlog/httpd.py` must NEVER import anything from `auditlog/cohorts.py`, or a circular import will result. This drove the decision to reimplement cohort-CSV-loading logic locally inside `httpd.py` (`load_cohort_configuration`) rather than importing `cohorts.load_cohort_phases`.
   - `auditlog/paths.py` helpers `canonical_path`, `auth_path` (used to look up the route table *before* reading a request body — enables auth-before-body-parsing), `dispatch_path` (path handed to the handler *after* the route decision) — per README: "HTTP routing keeps request-path matching in auditlog.paths so authentication and dispatch share one helper."
   - SQLite persistence: `sqlite3` stdlib module, `isolation_level=None` (autocommit mode so each `execute()` commits immediately without needing explicit `conn.commit()`), `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` (enables safe concurrent multi-reader/writer access, especially for the separate-process read test), one `sqlite3.Connection` per thread via `threading.local()` (since `sqlite3.Connection` is not safe to share across threads).
   - `http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler` / `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer` for the HTTP daemon; `protocol_version = "HTTP/1.0"` chosen deliberately to avoid HTTP/1.1 keep-alive body-draining edge cases (each response closes the connection automatically).
   - Bearer token auth: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, compared against a server-configured secret string; refusal (401) must happen strictly before the request body is read or the store is touched (verified by a dedicated test: `test_refusal_never_reaches_the_store`).
   - Testing patterns: `tempfile.mkdtemp()` + `shutil.rmtree` via `self.addCleanup(...)`; live HTTP server tests spin up a real `ThreadingHTTPServer`/`AuditHTTPServer` in a background daemon thread bound to an ephemeral port (`port=0`), using `http.client.HTTPConnection` to issue real requests; separate-process persistence verified via `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", script], cwd=REPO_ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)`.

   ```python
   """HTTP transport for the audit log: alias resolution, and the V1 daemon.

   `resolve_v2_alias_catalog` is the stable alias-resolution seam described
   below. Everything past it is the actual network daemon: a bearer-protected
   V1 `record`/`query`/`integrity` API backed by SQLite persistence. Only the
   routes in `ROUTE_ACTIONS` (mirroring `auditlog.policy.CANONICAL_V1_BEARER`)
   are ever dispatched to -- the V2 alias catalog in
   `auditlog.policy.build_v2_alias_catalog` is resolved here for callers such
   as `auditlog.cohorts`, but no V2 path is installed on the live server yet.
   """

   from __future__ import annotations

   import csv
   import json
   import sqlite3
   import threading
   from http import HTTPStatus
   from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
   from pathlib import Path
   from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit

   from auditlog.paths import auth_path, dispatch_path
   from auditlog.policy import CANONICAL_V1_BEARER
   from auditlog.service import AuditLogService, IntegrityError, SequenceError

   def resolve_v2_alias_catalog(catalog: tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool | None], ...], canonical_bearer: dict[tuple[str, str], bool]) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str, bool], ...]:
       """Resolve inherited aliases through their canonical V1 route keys."""

       resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str, bool]] = []
       for method, path, permission, requires_auth in catalog:
           if requires_auth is None:
               canonical_path = path.replace("/v2/", "/v1/", 1)
               requires_auth = canonical_bearer.get((method, canonical_path), True)
           resolved.append((method, path, permission, requires_auth))
       return tuple(resolved)

   # The only routes the live daemon dispatches to. Keys match
   # `auditlog.policy.CANONICAL_V1_BEARER` exactly: every installed route has a
   # canonical bearer requirement, and every canonical requirement names an
   # installed route. There is no V2 entry here -- installing the V2 alias
   # catalog at runtime is a later prompt's job.
   ROUTE_ACTIONS: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {
       ("POST", "/v1/entries"): "record",
       ("GET", "/v1/entries"): "query",
       ("GET", "/v1/integrity"): "integrity",
   }

   class SqliteEventStore:
       """SQLite-backed `EventStore` (see `auditlog.storage`).

       Unlike the CLI's single-writer JSON file, this store backs a daemon that
       may be read by several request threads -- and, for a separate OS process
       opening the same path, several processes -- at once. Autocommit mode plus
       WAL journaling means a writer's committed entry is immediately visible to
       any other connection that opens the same file afterward. Connections are
       kept one-per-thread because a `sqlite3.Connection` is not safe to share
       across threads.
       """

       def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
           self.path = path
           self._local = threading.local()
           self._init_schema()

       def _connection(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
           conn = getattr(self._local, "conn", None)
           if conn is None:
               conn = sqlite3.connect(self.path, isolation_level=None, timeout=30)
               conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
               self._local.conn = conn
           return conn

       def _init_schema(self) -> None:
           self._connection().execute(
               """
               CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entries (
                   sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
                   event_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                   actor TEXT NOT NULL,
                   action TEXT NOT NULL,
                   outcome TEXT NOT NULL,
                   recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                   source_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
                   metadata TEXT NOT NULL
               )
               """
           )

       def read_all(self) -> list[dict]:
           rows = self._connection().execute(
               "SELECT event_id, sequence, actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, "
               "source_version, metadata FROM entries ORDER BY sequence"
           ).fetchall()
           return [
               {
                   "event_id": event_id,
                   "sequence": sequence,
                   "actor": actor,
                   "action": action,
                   "outcome": outcome,
                   "recorded_at": recorded_at,
                   "source_version": source_version,
                   "metadata": json.loads(metadata),
               }
               for event_id, sequence, actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, source_version, metadata in rows
           ]

       def append(self, entry: dict) -> None:
           self._connection().execute(
               "INSERT INTO entries "
               "(sequence, event_id, actor, action, outcome, recorded_at, source_version, metadata) "
               "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
               (
                   entry["sequence"],
                   entry["event_id"],
                   entry["actor"],
                   entry["action"],
                   entry["outcome"],
                   entry["recorded_at"],
                   entry["source_version"],
                   json.dumps(entry.get("metadata", {})),
               ),
           )

   def load_cohort_configuration(csv_path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
       """Return {cohort: phase} for enabled rows of an upgrade-cohorts.csv file.

       Deterministic: `csv.DictReader` yields rows in file order, so the same
       file always produces the same dict. This duplicates the handful of
       lines in `auditlog.cohorts.load_cohort_phases` rather than importing it,
       because `auditlog.cohorts` already imports `resolve_v2_alias_catalog`
       from this module -- importing back would be circular. Loading this here
       only records configuration for a later phase to consult; it does not
       add a route, so it never changes what `ROUTE_ACTIONS` installs.
       """

       phases: dict[str, str] = {}
       with csv_path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
           for row in csv.DictReader(handle):
               if row["enabled"].strip().lower() == "true":
                   phases[row["cohort"]] = row["phase"]
       return phases

   def _event_payload(event) -> dict:
       return {
           "event_id": event.event_id,
           "sequence": event.sequence,
           "actor": event.actor,
           "action": event.action,
           "outcome": event.outcome,
           "recorded_at": event.recorded_at,
           "source_version": event.source_version,
           "metadata": event.metadata,
       }

   class AuditHTTPServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):
       """The V1 daemon's server: carries the service, bearer secret, and the
       (not-yet-installed) cohort configuration the request handler reads."""

       def __init__(
           self,
           server_address: tuple[str, int],
           RequestHandlerClass: type[BaseHTTPRequestHandler],
           service: AuditLogService,
           bearer_token: str,
           cohort_phases: dict[str, str],
       ) -> None:
           super().__init__(server_address, RequestHandlerClass)
           self.service = service
           self.bearer_token = bearer_token
           self.cohort_phases = cohort_phases
           self.write_lock = threading.Lock()

   class V1RequestHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
       """Dispatches only the routes in `ROUTE_ACTIONS`, each bearer-protected
       per `auditlog.policy.CANONICAL_V1_BEARER`."""

       protocol_version = "HTTP/1.0"
       server_version = "auditlogd/1"

       def log_message(self, format: str, *args) -> None:  # noqa: A002 - stdlib signature
           pass  # keep test output quiet; nothing here is a diagnostic signal

       def _send_json(self, status: HTTPStatus, payload: dict) -> None:
           body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
           self.send_response(status)
           self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
           self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
           self.end_headers()
           self.wfile.write(body)

       def _authorized(self, method: str, path: str) -> bool:
           if not CANONICAL_V1_BEARER.get((method, path), False):
               return True
           scheme, _, token = self.headers.get("Authorization", "").partition(" ")
           return scheme == "Bearer" and token == self.server.bearer_token

       def _dispatch(self) -> None:
           parsed = urlsplit(self.path)
           method = self.command

           # Route lookup and the auth decision happen before any body is read.
           auth_route = auth_path(parsed.path)
           if ROUTE_ACTIONS.get((method, auth_route)) is None:
               self._send_json(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": "no such route"})
               return
           if not self._authorized(method, auth_route):
               self._send_json(HTTPStatus.UNAUTHORIZED, {"error": "bearer token required"})
               return

           # Auth passed; the handler dispatches on the same path spelling.
           action = ROUTE_ACTIONS[(method, dispatch_path(parsed.path))]
           service = self.server.service

           if action == "record":
               self._handle_record(service)
           elif action == "query":
               self._handle_query(service, parse_qs(parsed.query))
           elif action == "integrity":
               self._handle_integrity(service)

       def _handle_record(self, service: AuditLogService) -> None:
           length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0) or 0)
           raw_body = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b"{}"
           try:
               payload = json.loads(raw_body or b"{}")
           except json.JSONDecodeError:
               self._send_json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": "invalid JSON body"})
               return
           try:
               with self.server.write_lock:
                   event = service.record(
                       payload["actor"],
                       payload["action"],
                       payload["outcome"],
                       metadata=payload.get("metadata"),
                       recorded_at=payload.get("recorded_at"),
                   )
           except KeyError as exc:
               self._send_json(HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, {"error": f"missing field {exc}"})
               return
           self._send_json(HTTPStatus.CREATED, _event_payload(event))

       def _handle_query(self, service: AuditLogService, query: dict[str, list[str]]) -> None:
           actor = query.get("actor", [None])[0]
           action = query.get("action", [None])[0]
           events = service.query(actor=actor, action=action)
           self._send_json(HTTPStatus.OK, {"entries": [_event_payload(event) for event in events]})

       def _handle_integrity(self, service: AuditLogService) -> None:
           try:
               events = service.verify()
           except (SequenceError, IntegrityError) as exc:
               self._send_json(HTTPStatus.CONFLICT, {"verified": False, "error": str(exc)})
               return
           self._send_json(HTTPStatus.OK, {"verified": True, "count": len(events)})

       def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - stdlib signature
           self._dispatch()

       def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - stdlib signature
           self._dispatch()

   def build_server(
       store_path: Path,
       bearer_token: str,
       cohorts_csv: Path | None = None,
       host: str = "127.0.0.1",
       port: int = 0,
   ) -> AuditHTTPServer:
       """Build (but do not start) the V1-only audit HTTP daemon.

       Persistence is `SqliteEventStore` at `store_path`. If `cohorts_csv` is
       given, its cohort-to-phase configuration is loaded once, deterministically
       (`load_cohort_configuration`) and kept on the server for a later phase to
       consult; it is never used to install a route here, so a cohort configured
       for "v2" still only ever reaches the V1 routes this daemon serves.
       """

       service = AuditLogService(SqliteEventStore(store_path))
       cohort_phases = load_cohort_configuration(cohorts_csv) if cohorts_csv is not None else {}
       return AuditHTTPServer((host, port), V1RequestHandler, service, bearer_token, cohort_phases)
   ```
   - Why important: this is the core deliverable of Phase C — SQLite persistence + bearer-protected V1 record/query/integrity routes, with V2 explicitly not installed, and deterministic cohort configuration loaded at server-build time.
   - Note the second edit I made to `_dispatch`: originally I had a wasteful throwaway call `dispatch_path(parsed.path)  # shares the lookup helper; same decision either way` whose result was discarded. I refactored it so `dispatch_path`'s result is actually used as the key for the final `ROUTE_ACTIONS[...]` lookup that determines the handler branch, making both `auth_path` and `dispatch_path` calls functionally meaningful (auth_path for the pre-body existence+auth check, dispatch_path for the actual dispatch decision).

   class LiveServerTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
       """Starts one real V1-only daemon per test against a temp SQLite store."""

       def setUp(self) -> None:
           self.tmp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
           self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.tmp_dir)
           self.server = build_server(
               self.tmp_dir / "store.sqlite3",
               bearer_token=TOKEN,
               cohorts_csv=FIXTURES / "upgrade-cohorts.csv",
               port=0,
           )
           self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)

           self.addCleanup(self._shutdown)

           self,
           method: str,
           path: str,
           *,
           token: str | None = None,
           body: dict | None = None,
       ) -> tuple[int, dict | None]:
           conn = HTTPConnection(self.host, self.port, timeout=5)
           try:

               conn.request(method, path, body=payload, headers=headers)
               response = conn.getresponse()
               raw = response.read()
               data = json.loads(raw) if raw else None
               return response.status, data
